images.title: Where two metro lines meet
images.purpose: Show the capsule at Hauz Khas where the Yellow Line and the Magenta Line meet, next to the two key symbols: the plain circle for a metro station and the capsule with two coloured dots for an interchange.
images.composition: A part of the metro map on the left, with a yellow line and a magenta line crossing at one capsule, and the key panel with its two symbols on the right.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816. At the top, centred at x 728 and y 60, the heading A part of the metro map in dark #1F2937 bold sans-serif (44 px). MAP PANEL: one rounded rectangle (corner radius 20 px), x 60 to 880 and y 110 to 720, white fill, dark #2B2B2B outline 3 px. YELLOW LINE: one vertical band 14 px wide centred at x 470, y 190 to 690, filled yellow #F0E442 with a thin dark outline (2 px). MAGENTA LINE: one horizontal band 14 px thick centred at y 420, x 100 to 840, filled reddish purple #CC79A7 with a thin dark outline (2 px). CAPSULE: one rounded rectangle 110 by 48 px (corner radius 24) centred at x 470 and y 420 (x 415 to 525, y 396 to 444), white fill, dark outline 4 px, holding two dots of radius 12 with a 2 px dark outline: a yellow #F0E442 dot centred at x 445 and y 420 and a reddish purple #CC79A7 dot centred at x 495 and y 420. CIRCLES: exactly 8 station circles of radius 14, white fill, dark outline 4 px: 2 above the capsule on the yellow line at x 470 and y 290 and y 350; 2 below it at x 470 and y 490 and y 550; 2 on the left on the magenta line at y 420 and x 260 and x 340; 2 on the right at y 420 and x 600 and x 680. LABELS ON THE MAP: Hauz Khas in dark bold (36 px), left aligned at x 530 and baseline y 376; Yellow Line in dark bold (30 px) centred at x 470 and y 160; Magenta Line in dark bold (30 px) centred at x 210 and y 475. TAG: one rounded rectangle 305 by 70 px at x 555 to 860 and y 520 to 590, white fill, amber #E69F00 outline 5 px, with the text Two lines meet here in dark bold (26 px), joined to the capsule by one dark 4 px arrow from x 590 and y 520 to x 525 and y 448, arrowhead at the capsule. KEY PANEL: one rounded rectangle (corner radius 20 px) at x 940 to 1400 and y 230 to 520, white fill, dark outline 4 px; the heading Key in dark bold (36 px) centred at x 1170 and y 280. Key row 1: the number 9 in dark bold (32 px) at x 975 and y 368, a plain white circle of radius 16 with a dark outline (4 px) centred at x 1030 and y 360, and the words Metro Station in dark bold (32 px) left aligned at x 1075 and baseline y 372. Key row 2: the number 10 in dark bold (32 px) at x 975 and y 448, a capsule 70 by 34 px (corner radius 17) centred at x 1050 and y 440 with white fill, dark outline 4 px and two dots of radius 9 (a yellow #F0E442 dot at x 1036 and y 440, a reddish purple #CC79A7 dot at x 1064 and y 440), and the words Interchange Line in dark bold (32 px) left aligned at x 1105 and baseline y 452. In all: 1 map panel, 2 lines, 1 capsule on the map, 8 circles, 1 tag, 1 key panel with 2 symbols. No other text and nothing else in the frame.
labels: A part of the metro map
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
a plain circle at the Hauz Khas crossing instead of the capsule with two coloured dots
any station name other than Hauz Khas, or any other line colour than yellow and magenta on the map
images.takeaway: A capsule with two coloured dots is an interchange: the Yellow Line and the Magenta Line meet at Hauz Khas, so you can change lines there. A plain circle is just a station.
images.description: A yellow line and a magenta line crossing at a capsule labelled Hauz Khas, with a key that shows a plain circle as Metro Station and a capsule as Interchange Line.
images.context: Concept image for Reading a Metro Map: Lines, Stations and Key. It follows the idea of the Delhi metro map and its key in your maths book and uses this concept's own example, Hauz Khas, where the Yellow Line and the Magenta Line meet.
images.teaching_notes: Let the student match the capsule on the map with symbol 10 in the key, and a circle with symbol 9. The slip to watch: thinking that two lines can be changed wherever they cross, without a capsule.

image_decisions.why: The capsule beside the key symbols lets the student match a symbol on the map with its meaning in the key, which words alone do not.
